- Chris Mayer's 100-bagger traits: high returns on capital (ROE of 15%+ in most years), a durable competitive advantage, a focus on ROIC and FCF, avoiding heavy debt so that drawdowns don't cause permanent impairment, and very long holding periods (most took 20–25 years; one summary says about 17 years at about 26% CAGR) — [Hedge Fund Alpha](https://hedgefundalpha.com/strategies/christopher-mayers-notes-100-baggers/); [TIP](https://www.theinvestorspodcast.com/articles/100-bagger-stocks/); [Outlook Business](https://www.outlookbusiness.com/hardbound/bagging-rights-2772)
- Small starting size: 8 of the top-10 Indian fastest creators (2016–21) started below ₹2,000 cr market cap — [Business Standard / MOSL](https://www.business-standard.com/amp/article/markets/reliance-industries-largest-wealth-creator-in-2016-21-says-motilal-oswal-121121401678_1.html)
- MOSL's 2024 study theme, "Creating Wealth Through Bruised Blue Chips", buys quality companies during temporary distress — [InvestmentGuru](https://investmentguruindia.com/newsdetail/motilal-oswal-29-th-annual-wealth-creation-study-2024-creating-wealth-through-bruised-blue-chips555308)

body:
`case_study:zee-essel-pledges-2019` | 2019-01-25 | tickers: ZEEL, DISHTV | confidence: verified

Zee Entertainment was a high-quality, cash-generative media franchise, but promoter Subhash Chandra's Essel group borrowed against Zee shares to fund infrastructure, power and other ventures. On 25 Jan 2019 Zee fell ~26-33% intraday on reports linking the group to an investigation and on lenders invoking pledges; Essel group listed stocks (Dish TV, Zee Media, Siti) fell 10-30%. Pledges rose to ~59% then ~90% of promoter holding; promoter debt ~Rs 7,000 cr (Oct 2019) after asset sales. Zee hit a ~6-year low in Sep-Oct 2019 (-60%+ from the ~Rs 600 Jan 2018 peak). Promoter stake fell from ~42% to ~4% as lenders and promoters sold. Later: a Zee FD/letter of comfort for group loans (Yes Bank) surfaced; Invesco fight (2021); the Sony merger collapsed (Jan 2024); SEBI orders on fund diversion (2023) and a separate Aug 2026 order barring Subhash Chandra and Punit Goenka for a year over an unauthorised Hyderabad land pledge (stock -13%). Visible flags: rising promoter pledge %, group holdco debt unrelated to Zee's business, MF FMPs lending against promoter shares, listed company comforts/guarantees for group debt, related-party advances. Lesson: a great business can be a bad stock if the promoter is levered elsewhere; pledges >25% and rising are a disqualifier.

**Lesson:** Pledge trend is a governance + forced-selling risk
**Spotted early by:** MF debt desks; pledge-tracking analysts
**Links:** illustrates -> `insight:promoter-pledge-group-contagion`, illustrates -> `insight:disqualifiers`
**Sources:** <https://business-standard.com/article/pf/zee-stock-crash-shows-why-you-should-avoid-firms-with-high-pledged-shares-119013100051_1.html> ; <https://www.businesstoday.in/amp/markets/company-stock/story/zee-shares-hit-over-6yr-low-as-promoters-increase-pledge-to-90-rebounds-debt-repayment-plan-231895-2019-10-07> ; <https://www.business-standard.com/article/markets/essel-group-shares-tumble-zee-tanks-12-dish-tv-hits-over-10-year-low-119092000243_1.html> ; <https://businesstoday.in/markets/stocks/story/zee-entertainment-shares-tank-13-amid-sebi-order-on-subhash-chandra-punit-goenka-546759-2026-08-03>

`insight:peak-hype-reversals` · confidence: verified

Cases and declines: Super Micro (-86%, 2024), Enphase (~-90%, 2022-25), Celsius (-73%, 2024), Tesla (-73%, 2021-23), Shopify (-87%, 2021-22), Palantir (-87% 2021-22; -36% from Nov 2025 peak while growing 85%), Novo (-73%, 2024-26), Constellation (-51%, 2025-26). Recurring tells visible before or at the top: (1) valuation extremes — P/S >30-100x (Palantir 137x; only 7 other software firms ever exceeded 100x sales and all fell >=70%), P/E ~100x (Celsius, Enphase); (2) gross-margin compression while revenue soars (SMCI 17% -> 11% -> 6%); (3) sell-in outrunning sell-through / distributor inventory build (Celsius-Pepsi, Enphase Europe); (4) demand dependent on a subsidy or rule (Enphase: NEM 3.0, 25D credit); (5) governance history (SMCI's 2018 delisting, prior SEC case; auditor resignation as the final alarm); (6) capex-heavy diversification by an asset-light company (Shopify logistics); (7) peak scarcity in a new category (Novo). Note: in most cases the business stayed real — the loss came from price paid and from one fragile assumption. Process rule: when two or more tells co-occur, cut size or require a much lower entry; never average down after an auditor resigns.

- **Links:** `case_study:super-micro-2023-2026`, `case_study:enphase-2016-2025`, `case_study:celsius-2020-2025`, `case_study:palantir-2022-2026`, `insight:disqualifiers`, `insight:avoid-ruin`
- **Sources:** [1](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/04/22/prediction-palantir-stock-could-fall-80-further/) · [2](https://www.fool.com/investing/2024/11/06/why-celsius-stock-crashed-today) · [3](https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/super-micro-shares-drop-ernst-young-resigns-amid-accounting-concerns)

body:
- Screener's "Borrowings" includes lease liabilities, so asset-light retailers look indebted.
- Goodwill from a PE buyout crushes reported ROE and ROCE. Use return on tangible equity.
- Ind AS 116 EBITDA overstates margins of rent-heavy models by 4–6 pp. Always find the pre-Ind AS number (company presentation, or EBITDA − lease cash outflow).
- Viral social-media "ground data" can be fake (the VMM guard-recruitment meme was disowned by the company).
- Payback and SSSG are company-defined. Read the definition before quoting them.
- (v1.1) **Cost-plus transfer pricing caps margins.** Exports sold to the parent at cost + x% do not gain from a weak rupee. The parent captures it.
- (v1.1) **High ROCE can be borrowed from the group's balance sheet.** If the constrained product is made by a sister company, the listed entity's capital looks small.
- (v1.1) **Cost allocations from the parent can step up without notice** (Cummins: support services ₹111 → ₹223 cr in a year, then a further Q2 "true-up"). Read the other-expenses note every year, and the call's "one-offs" answer every quarter.
- (v1.1) **Company "ranges" can hide the number.** "DC = 30–40% of power gen" is ±₹130 cr a quarter, wide enough to hide a slowdown in the rest of the business.
- (v1.2) **US GAAP gross margin is not comparable across retailers.** Some put occupancy, distribution and buying in COGS (FIVE); others put them in SG&A. Compare operating margin, or rebuild merchandise margin.
- (v1.2) **One-off credits inside COGS.** FIVE's Q2 FY26 GAAP gross margin of 48.5% included a $163.6M tariff refund. Trailing GAAP EPS screens are wrong for four quarters. Always read the Ex-99.1 reconciliation.
- (v1.2) **Ownership-filing false alarms.** Vanguard's 13G/A shows 0% after its Jan-2026 realignment. The 13F still shows the shares.
- (v1.2) **"Average sales per store" usually counts only stores open the full year.** Also compute total sales ÷ average store count.
- (v1.2) **FCF in a slowdown-of-openings year is flattered** (capex and working-capital timing). Normalise before using it.
- (v1.2) **Tool notes:** use `sec_fetch.py doc T ACC --file NAME --text` for exhibits; `holdings13f` value can misparse (use shares); confirm the insider "non-10b5-1" flag on the form.
- (v1.1) **Tool note:** `tools/nse_fetch.py transcripts SYMBOL --download DIR` ignores `--from/--to` and downloads everything. List first, then fetch only the URLs you need.
- (v1.3) **"Decadal-low GNPA" can be write-off driven.** Rebuild the NPA walk: at Federal Bank Q2 FY27 write-offs (₹498 cr) exceeded fresh slippage (₹420 cr).
- (v1.3) **Special funding windows inflate both sides.** FCNR-backed loans turned +4% core retail growth into +18% headline.
- (v1.3) **PCR can be bought with a windfall.** A one-time tax-refund gain funded a buffer provision; PCR 76.6% → 87%.
- (v1.3) **Undiluted P/B and ROE flatter a bank with warrants outstanding.** Put the dilution in the denominator first.
- (v1.3) **Conservative guidance makes a credibility score look excellent.** Measure guidance bias, and compare with peers.
- (v1.3) **Rating-agency and company KPI definitions differ** (credit cost 67 bp vs 41 bp; "top-20 group" vs "top-20 borrowers"). Copy the definition with the number.
- (v1.3) **Tool notes:** `nse_fetch.py results` is stale after Dec-2024 (use `integrated`); bank websites may be behind a bot wall (Pillar 3, some transcripts) — fetch by hand and pass `--local`; pdftotext scrambles multi-series deck charts (prefer XBRL and press releases).

body:
- **What the market appears to price:** roughly even odds that IMCL keeps the hospital on workable terms (17x vs peers 48x).
- **Our view:** **no claimable mispricing.** Our evidence leans slightly *negative* versus the company's framing (omitted expiry; "remained
  compliant"; GNCTD abstaining and leaving board seats empty; MD gap), and positive versus a naive "takeover" fear (net cash ₹57/share floor; courts and
  governments usually prefer stricter terms over closing a 700-bed hospital). The tails are **above** the class base rate for documented reasons.
- **What would prove us wrong (upside):** a disclosed 30-year renewal near IMCL's ask without a retrospective claim — then the peer gap (0.35x) is
  the opportunity the market under-priced.
- **What would prove us wrong (downside):** a handover order — then even our 20% blow-up weight was too low.
- **Base-class departure (card §5):** P(≥3x) 7% vs 21% class; P(≤0.5x) 26% vs 11%; P(blow-up) 20% vs 15%. Tails anchored at **w = 0.3** (below the
  0.5 default) with a written evidence note, because anchoring at 0.5 would *lower* the blow-up probability toward a class that has no lease-expiry
  information. First card where anchoring moves the tails **down** (and EV up: 1.35x → 1.39x).

**Inputs (L8 step 1):** close ₹11.71 on 23-Nov-2026 (NSE bhavcopy = Yahoo; screener ₹11.7 — 3 sources); shares 177.95 cr; net worth ₹2,676 cr
(XBRL = deck); assumed **₹500 cr equity raise at ₹11** in FY28 (45.45 cr shares) `[EST]`; FY-end P/Bs only 3 (listed Jul-2023): Mar-24 1.74x,
Mar-25 0.82x, Mar-26 0.66x `[YH ÷ SCR; Yahoo pre-Nov-2025 closes are rights-adjusted; 1 src]`; peers median 1.01x; 6-month ADV ₹12.0 cr mean / ₹6.3 cr
median; CoE 12.5% (India default, for comparability), g 5%, σ 0.35.
**Scenarios (written before the outputs; 10-year linear ROE paths):** bear 30% (prolonged stress, second cycle: ROE −4% → 8%, exit 0.6x); base 40%
(slow recovery: 4% → 13%, exit 0.9x); bull 15% (guidance broadly met: 10% → 15%, exit 1.4x); blow-up 15% at 0.15x (a second cycle loss on CET1 book
₹1,907 cr at 10.9x leverage forces a deeply discounted raise or an RBI-led merger).
**Outputs:** P/B 0.78x (0.82x diluted); **ROE needed forever 11.2%** (13.2% on CET1 book, `UTKARSHBNK_cet1book_worksheet.md`); base-case IRR **12.0%**
= the 12% hurdle; 5-year multiples bear 0.68x / base 1.46x / bull 2.85x / blow-up 0.15x; **EV 1.24x raw** vs hurdle 1.76x; P(≥2x) 20%, P(≥3x) 7%,
P(≤0.5x) 21%, P(blow-up) 15%; probability-weighted RIM value ₹7.9 (−32%). Book stress: an extra 2% loan loss (post-tax) = 9% of book; 5% = 23%.
**Exit-multiple bet:** RIM-consistent P/B at year 5: bear 0.29x vs 0.60x used (the bear exit is *generous* — flagged by the tool), base 1.00x vs
0.90x, bull 1.41x vs 1.40x. As in every card (L21, L36), the exit multiple and the ROE path are the binding choices; here the bear exit is the
optimistic assumption, which means the true left tail is, if anything, fatter.
**Temperature:** own history insufficient (n = 3); **COOL vs SFB peers (0.82x of median)**; on CET1 book it is at the peer median.
**CET1-book sensitivity** (same scenarios, CET1 book; harsh because the exit P/Bs are then applied to CET1 book): EV 0.94x, base IRR 10.9%.
